user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message to my daughter, but it just won’t go through. I’m not very good with these things, so I’m hoping you can help me fix it.

I can help you with that. To assist you better, I need to identify your account. Could you please provide me with your phone number or your full name along with your date of birth? This will help me check your account and line status.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you also need my date of birth?
Yes, for verification purposes, I need your full name and date of birth. Could you please provide your date of birth as well?
Of course, my date of birth is January 15, 1960. Let me know if you need anything else.

I found an account under the phone number you provided, but the date of birth on record is June 15, 1985, which does not match the date you gave me. Could you please confirm if the phone number or the date of birth might be different? This is to ensure I access the correct account to assist you with your picture messaging issue.

Oh dear, I’m sure my phone number is 555-123-2002, and my birthday is definitely January 15, 1960. I’m not sure why it wouldn’t match. Is there anything else I can check or do on my end to help? I really just want to get these pictures sent to my daughter.

Since the date of birth you provided does not match the one on record for the phone number 555-123-2002, I am unable to access your account for security reasons. 

If you want, I can still help you troubleshoot the picture messaging issue on your phone without accessing your account details. Would you like me to proceed with that?

Yes, please! I just want to be able to send my pictures again. I don’t really understand all the technical stuff, so I’d appreciate any help you can give me, even if you can’t get into my account. What should I do next?

To start troubleshooting your picture messaging issue, I will guide you through some checks on your phone to understand the current status of your cellular service and mobile data, which are essential for sending picture messages.

First, please check the status bar on your phone and tell me what icons or indicators you see at the top of your screen. This includes things like signal strength bars, airplane mode, Wi-Fi connection, or any other symbols.

At the top of my screen, I see a signal bar that looks pretty low, something that says “2G,” and a little icon that I think means mobile data is on. My battery is at 80%. I don’t see anything about airplane mode or Wi-Fi. Is that helpful?

Thank you for the information. The "2G" indicator suggests your phone is currently connected to a 2G network, which is generally not suitable for sending picture messages (MMS). Picture messages typically require at least a 3G or higher network connection.

I can help you change your phone's network mode preference to allow it to connect to 4G or 5G networks, which should improve your ability to send picture messages.

Would you like me to proceed with changing your network mode preference to 4G/5G?

Oh, I see. Yes, please go ahead and help me change it to 4G or 5G—whatever will help me send my pictures. Will this mess up anything else on my phone? I just want to make sure I don’t lose anything important.

Changing your network mode preference to 4G/5G will not mess up anything on your phone or cause you to lose any data. It simply allows your phone to connect to faster and more modern cellular networks, which should help with sending picture messages and improve overall data performance.

I will proceed to change your network mode preference to 4G/5G now.
